source.title: Multi-View Feature Representation for Dialogue Generation with Bidirectional Distillation
source.authors: Shaoxiong Feng; Xuancheng Ren; Kan Li; Xu Sun

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper; no material cutoff or garbling prevents reading the relevant sections.
record.tranche_reason: The paper extends a parameter-perturbation analysis of local minima to dialogue-generation models, reporting test-loss changes under Gaussian parameter noise. It does not test classification error or the training-test error gap.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-loss robustness to noisy training data and Gaussian parameter perturbations. Only the perturbation analysis bears on V7’s generalization-measure theme; the other reported evaluations concern dialogue response quality or noise robustness and do not test the listed versions.
record.test_reason: The study evaluates its dialogue-training method and uses the premise that wider minima imply better generalization to interpret parameter robustness. It does not test any listed version: Figure 4 measures test-loss sensitivity to unscaled Gaussian parameter noise, not V7's magnitude-aware sharpness or its relationship with training–test gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that MRBD improves dialogue-model generalization and interpret its lower parameter-perturbation sensitivity as evidence of wider local minima. That interpretation does not establish V7's specified sharpness–generalization-gap relationship.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies dialogue generation and uses independent Gaussian parameter perturbations to examine changes in test loss; it does not reproduce the listed classification studies’ methods or measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported perturbation analysis varies the standard deviation σ of independent Gaussian noise added to learned parameters.

fits_no_version.finding: On DailyDialog, the authors report that MRBD's test loss changes less under independent Gaussian parameter perturbations than baseline losses (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MRBD-trained dialogue models are less sensitive to unscaled Gaussian parameter noise than the tested baselines.

fits_no_version.finding: MRBD and Co-Teaching show greater test-loss robustness when training responses are randomly replaced (Figure 3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dialogue distillation methods using separate training subsets can improve robustness to corrupted training responses.

record.problems: The relevant perturbation findings are presented in a figure without numerical values in the text. The paper reports test-loss sensitivity, not a measured training-test error gap.
record.rows_left_out: No rows retained: Figure 4 is described qualitatively, without numerical values, and the reported test-loss sensitivity does not measure V7’s specified magnitude-aware perturbation threshold or training-test gap.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy. Randomly replacing dialogue responses does not establish these outcomes.
Test error as network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under limited or broader tuning; Adam is used without an optimizer comparison.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that mitigate them.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training-set sizes and regularization settings; dropout is fixed at 0.1.

Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, training-error thresholds, correlation with training–test gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by label-memorization influence versus removing equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: There are no extracted rows to fix. The omitted perturbation result is already declared in rows_left_out and does not warrant a V7 verdict. The Figure 4 paraphrase is supported by the supplied text, despite a line break splitting the word 'perturbations'.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large-batch training and its generalization gap.

Magnitude-scaled perturbations, training-error rise, training-test gaps, and comparisons with norm- and margin-based measures are not tested. The paper uses Gaussian parameter noise and reports test-loss sensitivity for dialogue models.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
